newsitem.title: JORDAN: PSA rules out merger with Renault.
newsitem.headline: PSA rules out merger with Renault.

text.p: PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet has reiterated his opposition to a merger with domestic rival Renault SA.

The idea was raised last week in a commentary in the magazine L'Express by former president Valery Giscard d'Estaing. Calvet had served as chief of staff to Giscard d'Estaing in the early 1970s when the latter was finance minister.
"This idea of a friendly alliance seems totally inconceivable to those on the inside," he told reporters during a presentation on Friday of the Peugeot 406 in Aqaba.
He said he agreed on this point with Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer, who said recently that a merger of the two French companies would reduce overall sales volumes and market share.
But Calvet said he was keen to develop cooperation between the two companies "in areas where we'd better as two than one" or where there was "usefulness" on technical matters.

He said the Peugeot group and Renault hold monthly meetings to discuss issues that affect them both. "We hold a number of common positions," he said. "I have the highest regard for my counterpart at Renault...and if there's scope to work together more, I would do it."

Talk of a merger between the two companies was revived by Renault's difficulties. Last week it reported a 5.25 billion franc ($920.6 million) net loss for 1996, including 3.91 billion francs in restructuring charges to downsize its operations in Europe.
Asked to comment on Renault's results, Calvet said it appeared Schweitzer had showed his willingness to take the situation in hand.
The Peugeot group is expected to issue its 1996 results next month.
-- Jacques Servant, Paris Newsroom, +33 1 4221 5452 ($ = 5.702 French Francs)
